[[Swaziland]] sent a delegation to compete at the [[2008 Summer Olympics]] held in [[Beijing]], [[People's Republic of China]] from August 8–24, 2008.  This was the Kingdom's eighth appearance at a [[Summer Olympic Games]].  The Swazi delegation to Beijing consisted of four competitors, two [[track and field]] athletes; [[Isaiah Msibi]] and [[Temalangeni Dlamini]]; and two [[swimming (sport)|swimmers]]; [[Luke Hall (swimmer)|Luke Hall]] and [[Senele Dlamini]].  None of the four advanced beyond the first round of their respective events.

==Background==
The [[Swaziland Olympic and Commonwealth Games Association]] was recognized by the [[International Olympic Committee]] on 1 January 1972.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/eswatini|title=Eswatini – National Olympic Committee (NOC)|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=19 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181003181813/https://www.olympic.org/eswatini|archive-date=2018-10-03|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  Swaziland first sent a delegation to the [[Summer Olympic Games]] at the [[1972 Summer Olympics]].<ref name="SWZSR">{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/SWZ/|title=Swaziland|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=19 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160624213825/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/SWZ/|archive-date=2016-06-24|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  They did not send a delegation in [[1976 Summer Olympics|1976]], and participated in the United States-led boycott of the [[1980 Summer Olympics]];<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1984/05/10/world/54-boycotted-in-1980.html|title=54 Boycotted in 1980|date=10 May 1984|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180130091021/http://www.nytimes.com/1984/05/10/world/54-boycotted-in-1980.html|archive-date=2018-01-30|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref> but have participated in every Summer Olympics since the [[1984 Summer Olympics|1984 Los Angeles Olympics]].<ref name="SWASR">{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/SWZ/|title=Swaziland|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160624213825/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/SWZ/|archive-date=2016-06-24|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  This made Beijing Swaziland's eighth appearance at a Summer Olympiad.<ref name="SWZSR" />  The 2008 Summer Olympics were held from 8–24 August 2008; a total of 10,942 athletes represented 204 [[National Olympic Committees]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/beijing-2008|title=Beijing 2008 Summer Olympics – results & video highlights|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=13 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180808185306/https://www.olympic.org/beijing-2008|archive-date=2018-08-08|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  The Swazi delegation to Beijing consisted of four competitors, two [[track and field]] athletes; [[Isaiah Msibi]] and [[Temalangeni Dlamini]]; and two [[swimming (sport)|swimmers]]; [[Luke Hall (swimmer)|Luke Hall]] and [[Senele Dlamini]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/SWZ/summer/2008/|title=Swaziland at the 2008 Beijing Summer Games|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181024232427/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/SWZ/summer/2008/|archive-date=2018-10-24|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  Temalangeni Dlamini was chosen as the flag-bearer for the [[2008 Summer Olympics opening ceremony|opening ceremony]],<ref name="SWZSR" /> while Hall was selected to do the same at the [[2008 Summer Olympics closing ceremony|closing ceremony]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stillmed.olympic.org/Documents/Reports/EN/en_report_1362.pdf|title=Closing Ceremony Flag Bearers|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=24 October 2018}}</ref>

==Athletics==
{{main|Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}

Temalangeni Dlamini was 21 years old at the time of the Beijing Olympics and was making her debut in Olympic competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/dl/temalangeni-dlamini-1.html|title=Temalangeni Dlamini Bio, Stats, and Results|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181024232345/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/dl/temalangeni-dlamini-1.html|archive-date=2018-10-24|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/temalangeni-dlamini|title=Temalangeni DLAMINI – Olympic Athletics – Swaziland|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161006021541/https://www.olympic.org/temalangeni-dlamini|archive-date=2016-10-06|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  On 16 August, she participated in the heats of the [[Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's 400 metres|women's 400 meters]], and was drawn into heat seven.  She finished her heat in a time of 59.91 seconds, seventh and last in her heat, over nine seconds behind the heat's winner, [[Shericka Williams]] of [[Jamaica at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Jamaica]], and was eliminated from the competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2008/ATH/womens-400-metres-round-one.html|title=Athletics at the 2008 Beijing Summer Games: Women's 400 metres Round One|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181024232406/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2008/ATH/womens-400-metres-round-one.html|archive-date=2018-10-24|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  The gold medal was eventually won by [[Christine Ohuruogu]] of [[Great Britain at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Great Britain]] in 49.62 seconds, the silver by Williams, and the bronze medal was taken by [[Sanya Richards-Ross]] of the [[United States at the 2008 Summer Olympics|United States]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2008/ATH/womens-400-metres.html|title=Athletics at the 2008 Beijing Summer Games: Women's 400 metres|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180915042629/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2008/ATH/womens-400-metres.html|archive-date=2018-09-15|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/beijing-2008/athletics/400m-women|title=Beijing 2008 400m women – Olympic Athletics|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181024232042/https://www.olympic.org/beijing-2008/athletics/400m-women|archive-date=2018-10-24|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

Isaiah Msibi was 24 years old at the time, and likewise making his first Olympic appearance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ms/isaiah-msibi-1.html|title=Isaiah Msibi Bio, Stats, and Results|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181013070312/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ms/isaiah-msibi-1.html|archive-date=2018-10-13|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/isaiah-msibi|title=Isaiah MSIBI – Olympic Athletics – Swaziland|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161006014615/https://www.olympic.org/isaiah-msibi|archive-date=2016-10-06|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  On 15 August, he took part in the [[Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's 1500 metres|men's 1500 meters]] and finished the first round race in 3 minutes and 51.35 seconds, 12th in his heat, and was eliminated from the competition.<ref name="Men's1500">{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/beijing-2008/athletics/1500m-men|title=Beijing 2008 1500m men – Olympic Beijing 2008 Athletics|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181024231949/https://www.olympic.org/beijing-2008/athletics/1500m-men|archive-date=2018-10-24|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  The gold medal was eventually won in 3 minutes and 33.11 seconds by [[Asbel Kiprop]] of [[Morocco at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Morocco]], the silver by [[Nick Willis]] of [[New Zealand at the 2008 Summer Olympics|New Zealand]], and the bronze was won by [[France at the 2008 Summer Olympics|France]]'s [[Mehdi Baala]].<ref name="Men's1500" />

==Swimming==
{{main|Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics}}

Luke Hall was 19 years old at the time of the Beijing Olympics, and would later go on to represent [[Swaziland at the 2012 Summer Olympics|Swaziland]] again four years later in the [[2012 Summer Olympics|2012 London Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ha/luke-hall-1.html|title=Luke Hall Bio, Stats, and Results|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161019020805/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ha/luke-hall-1.html|archive-date=2016-10-19|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/luke-hall|title=Luke HALL – Olympic Swimming – Swaziland|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005182005/https://www.olympic.org/luke-hall|archive-date=2016-10-05|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  On 14 August, he took part in the first round of the [[Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's 50 metre freestyle|men's 50 meter freestyle]], a race he finished in 24.41 seconds, good for 60th place out of 97 athletes, and he was eliminated as only the top 16 advanced to the semifinals.<ref name="Men's50m">{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/beijing-2008/swimming/50m-freestyle-men|title=Beijing 2008 50m freestyle men – Olympic Beijing 2008 Swimming|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702093612/https://www.olympic.org/beijing-2008/swimming/50m-freestyle-men|archive-date=2018-07-02|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  The gold medal was won by [[César Cielo]] of [[Brazil at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Brazil]] in 21.30 seconds, the silver and bronze medals were both won by Frenchmen, the silver by [[Amaury Leveaux]] and the bronze by [[Alain Bernard]].<ref name="Men's50m" /> Four years later, in the same event, Hall came in 36th place.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2012/SWI/mens-50-metres-freestyle.html|title=Swimming at the 2012 London Summer Games: Men's 50 metres Freestyle|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180818214509/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2012/SWI/mens-50-metres-freestyle.html|archive-date=2018-08-18|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

Senele Dlamini was 16 years old at the time of these Olympics, and was making her Olympic debut.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/dl/senele-dlamini-1.html|title=Senele Dlamini Bio, Stats, and Results|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181024232317/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/dl/senele-dlamini-1.html|archive-date=2018-10-24|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/senele-dlamini|title=Senele DLAMINI – Olympic Swimming – Swaziland|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181024232330/https://www.olympic.org/senele-dlamini|archive-date=2018-10-24|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  She finished the first round of the [[Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's 50 metre freestyle|women's 50 meter freestyle]] in 28.70 seconds, which was 61st place out of 90 competitors.  Similarly to the men's race, only the top 16 could advance to the semifinals, and Dlamini was eliminated from the competition.<ref name="50FreeWomen">{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/beijing-2008/swimming/50m-freestyle-women|title=Beijing 2008 50m freestyle women – Olympic Beijing 2008 Swimming|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181024232319/https://www.olympic.org/beijing-2008/swimming/50m-freestyle-women|archive-date=2018-10-24|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  The gold medal was eventually won in the finals in 24.06 seconds by [[Britta Steffen]] of [[Germany at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Germany]], the silver medal was earned by [[Dara Torres]] of the United States, and the bronze medal was taken by [[Cate Campbell]] of [[Australia at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Australia]].<ref name="50FreeWomen" />
